title: WTF Media Architecture Ledger
subtitle: Evidence-led inventory, operating boundaries, and release documentation contract

statusLegend.label: Implemented source
statusLegend.description: Tracked code or schema exists; no live runtime is implied.

statusLegend.label: Locally verified
statusLegend.description: A repository-owned local test or command has evidence.

statusLegend.label: Declared config
statusLegend.description: A binding or configuration is declared in source; provisioning is unverified.

statusLegend.label: Historical record
statusLegend.description: A prior document records an event; this inventory did not re-probe it.

statusLegend.label: Planned / owner-gated

releaseEvents.meaning: A package version only; it is not a deployment, product release, or OTA artifact.
The web package defines the build and verifier surface; historic changelog entries are not current deployment proof.
Worker bindings are declared in source; this inventory does not assert that the configured account resources are current.
A repository-local, read-only STDIO scaffold. It is not installed globally, hosted, published, or OTA-capable.

sections.title: Purpose, scope, and evidence rule
sections.summary: This ledger is the current repository architecture inventory. It distinguishes code, local checks, historical notes, configuration declarations, and owner-gated plans rather than collapsing them into a single green status.

facts.label: Canonical artifact
facts.value: Generated offline from this source ledger and repository metadata

facts.label: No hidden runtime inference
facts.value: A version, binding, test pass, or historic document does not prove a live deployment

body: Every inventory claim names a source and a next gate. Runtime configuration, credentials, account identifiers, and private media are deliberately absent.

The generator fingerprints selected tracked architecture sources. A relevant reviewed code, configuration, workflow, or release change makes the rendered artifacts stale until a maintainer reviews and regenerates them; untracked drafts are deliberately excluded.

sections.title: Phase 1 access decision
sections.summary: Repository Phase 1 is a public compatibility and proof-harness release. It is not gated by Cloudflare Zero Trust, Access Applications, Access policies, or D1 operator provisioning.

facts.label: Public verifier
facts.value: Runs local build, browser, visual, privacy, rollback, and contract evidence without a live external service

facts.label: Protected scope
facts.value: Middleware treats /ops as a separate operator boundary; public routes remain outside that branch

body: This is an exemption from a missing dependency, not a production authorization bypass. Public Phase 1 acceptance must remain credential- and network-independent.
The client-facing phrase ‘Phase 1’ is a delivery-track label. It does not turn modeled operator access into a live prerequisite or retroactively alter repository Phase 1 acceptance.

sections.title: Repository topology and ownership boundaries
sections.summary: The repository is a modular web-and-edge system: Next.js presents public and operator shells, while Cloudflare code owns retrieval, storage, ingestion, and future protected APIs.

facts.label: Web
facts.value: Next.js App Router, React, TypeScript, Tailwind, browser and unit verification

facts.label: Edge
facts.value: Worker source, D1 migrations, R2, KV, Queue, Vectorize, and Workers AI bindings

facts.label: Agentic package
facts.value: Repository-local read-only MCP scaffold

body: The browser must not receive Worker secrets, account tokens, raw provider payloads, or private provenance paths. Public catalogue behavior and internal operations share evidence primitives but retain separate narratives and permissions.

Vercel deployment configuration is not asserted by this checkout. Existing Cloudflare deployment descriptions are historical records unless a separately approved live probe supplies a redacted receipt.

sections.title: Public application and route boundary
sections.summary: The public shell preserves catalogue discovery, episode detail, connections, and Ask WTF without exposing the operator control-room model.

facts.label: Protected route separation
facts.value: Only /ops and recovery-related routes enter the operator middleware path

facts.label: Public evidence contract
facts.value: Citations only expose allowlisted public metadata and validated YouTube timing

body: Public source links never invent timestamps and must not expose uncut storage locations, local paths, transcript bodies, or operator-only identifiers.
The public shell is a read-only projection. It is not evidence that future production, calendar, analytics, or seat-management systems have canonical data.

sections.title: Ask WTF request path and grounding contract
sections.summary: The public chat route keeps the browser on the Next.js boundary and forwards server-side to the edge retrieval service using a server-only secret.

facts.label: Proxy boundary
facts.value: The Next route forwards bounded requests server-to-server and returns safe error shapes

facts.label: Retrieval sources
facts.value: Workers AI embeds and answers; Vectorize returns candidate passages; citations are validated before response

body: The historic Cloudflare infrastructure note records a prior deployment narrative, but this inventory does not call a live endpoint. Treat it as context, not a fresh operational receipt.
A direct Worker chat request is designed to fail without the server-only edge secret. The source tree does not include that value.

sections.title: Cloudflare resource declaration inventory
sections.summary: The Worker configuration declares Workers AI, Vectorize, KV, R2, Queue/DLQ behavior, D1, observability, and a public Worker entrypoint. It does not prove current account provisioning or a deployed binding set.

facts.label: Declared bindings
facts.value: AI, VECTORIZE, WTFMEDIA_STATE, CATALOGUE, INGEST_QUEUE, DB

facts.label: Observability
facts.value: Enabled in Worker configuration; no live logs or alerts are evidenced here

body: Resource names and binding identifiers are useful configuration evidence. They are not account credentials and do not demonstrate that a particular dashboard or resource currently exists.
Environment-specific Access settings, protected hostnames, audiences, JWKS URLs, and an explicit cron trigger are absent from the committed Worker configuration.

sections.title: Worker routes, queue wiring, and scheduler limits
sections.summary: The Worker has an active fetch path and legacy queue behavior. The Phase 3 transcript consumer and scheduled helpers exist as source but are not wired into the exported runtime entrypoint.

facts.label: Current entrypoint
facts.value: Fetch plus legacy queue consumer are exported

facts.label: Held integrations
facts.value: Transcript consumer and scheduled YouTube/retention helpers require explicit entrypoint, binding, and cron work

body: This is a release blocker for live Phase 3 operation. Isolated function tests do not establish deployed queue dispatch, DLQ behavior, cron operation, or asset-confirm handoff.
A future owner-approved slice must add deployless entrypoint tests before a separate deployment authorization is considered.

sections.title: D1 and the provenance domain
sections.summary: Migrations model operator access, audit history, and a provenance spine of episodes, external identities, source assets, transcript versions, alignments, citations, and ingestion jobs.

facts.label: Access and audit schema
facts.value: Operator, role-transfer, invitation-approval, and audit migrations are present

facts.label: Provenance schema
facts.value: Migration 0005 and typed DAL define the Phase 3 graph

body: Schema and local migration tests provide source and local evidence only. No remote migration was inspected, applied, or inferred by this ledger.
The canonical model must remain the source for provenance and workflow claims; UI fixtures cannot become a competing record store.

sections.title: R2 asset vault and upload lifecycle
sections.summary: The repository contains intent, upload, and confirm handlers with signed ticket checks, metadata validation, canonical storage keys, D1 registration, and audit events. It is not yet a production-scale media upload design.

facts.label: Handler surface
facts.value: Intent, stream, and confirmation routes are protected by operator policy

facts.label: Known hold
facts.value: The current handler buffers the request body and ticket state is not durably single-use

body: The current tests prove bounded local behavior, including size and hash checks. They do not establish safe large-media streaming, durable replay prevention, remote object integrity, or a configured asset handoff.
No uncut audio or private vault object is represented in this document.

sections.title: Transcript, queue, and Vectorize lifecycle
sections.summary: The local pipeline parses diarized transcript inputs, validates timing, stages versions, creates embeddings, and models vector cutover. Runtime wiring and remote failure evidence are still held.

facts.label: Pipeline code
facts.value: Transcript parsing, chunking, embeddings, version staging, and queue consumer are present

facts.label: Safety posture
facts.value: Malformed, missing, and unavailable asset cases have focused local tests

body: A vector projection is rebuildable; canonical provenance and stored source assets are the evidence-bearing records. Version activation must not be described as durable until D1, Vectorize, and queue failure behavior are tested together.
There is no claim of remotely ingested transcripts or live DLQ inspection.

sections.title: YouTube OAuth and scheduled synchronization
sections.summary: YouTube adapter code is bearer-token oriented and manual sync fails closed while OAuth is not connected. The account connection, encrypted credential lifecycle, consent, revocation, approved channels, and scheduler activation are separate work.

facts.label: Current safe behavior
facts.value: Manual sync reports oauth_not_configured before job or audit mutation

facts.label: Delivery owner
facts.value: OAuth-only YouTube provider is tracked separately

body: API-key fallback is not the intended connection model. Credentials and refresh tokens remain outside the repository, and a version or mocked adapter test cannot establish account connectivity.
A future schedule must advance cache state only after durable canonical persistence succeeds.

sections.title: Timeline alignment, citations, and dual playback
sections.summary: Public citation parsing and dual-playback mapping only accept allowlisted source data and valid YouTube identifiers. Uncut playback stays unavailable when trusted alignment and access are absent.

facts.label: Public projection
facts.value: Unexpected source fields and private paths are removed before client rendering

facts.label: Alignment engine
facts.value: Inverted, incomplete, and overlapping intervals are rejected rather than guessed

body: The Ask WTF YouTube/Uncut option is an evidence-led mode switch, not permission to reveal a private source. It must render an honest unavailable state where the underlying mapping or access proof does not exist.
Persisted alignment validation and a configured-asset integration test remain future requirements.

sections.title: WTF OS operator shell and truthful empty states
sections.summary: The repository contains a protected-appearance shell, navigation projection, recovery view, operator roster UI, production chrome, audit page, and operator API seams. These surfaces must not fabricate records or healthy integrations.

facts.label: Operator routes
facts.value: /ops, /ops/production, /ops/operators, and /ops/audit are modeled

facts.label: Truthful calendar
facts.value: Production UI is explicitly chrome until a canonical workflow store exists

body: A visible operator page is not a live protected application. Until a server-backed projection exists, its state must be unknown, unavailable, or not activated—not a made-up dashboard.
Current untracked operator drafts are excluded from the ledger and release evidence until individually reviewed and committed.

sections.title: Access, seats, RBAC, and local development seam
sections.summary: Future access is modeled as verified identity plus a fresh active D1 operator role. The role policy, single transferable super-admin seat, invitation approvals, audit behavior, and protected navigation are in source.

facts.label: Role model
facts.value: super_admin, admin, and editor are allowlisted with route-level capability checks

facts.label: Seat invariants
facts.value: A super-admin transfer guard and invitation approval model are migrated locally

facts.label: Local context
facts.value: Loopback development may generate an HMAC-signed preview context only in development with an explicit local secret

body: The local HMAC seam is a rendering/test harness. It is not Cloudflare Access, a user session, an Access Application, a policy, or production authorization.
No personally identifying roster details are copied into this ledger. A modeled seat is not evidence of a real account assignment.

sections.title: Cloudflare Zero Trust activation workstream
sections.summary: Live operator activation is a distinct, owner-approved workstream after public Phase 1. It cannot be inferred from local JWT verification code, symbolic schemas, or UI fixtures.

facts.label: Missing repository evidence
facts.value: No committed Access Application or policy configuration, protected hostname, issuer/audience/JWKS values, or environment-specific OPS settings

facts.label: Required proof
facts.value: Owner-approved valid, expired, forged, wrong-audience, inactive-role, cache/DTO, logout, revocation, and transfer tests

body: Do not deploy a Worker, configure an Access Application or policy, seed real seats, bind remote assets, or add credentials as part of this documentation change.
Before future route wiring, legacy header-trusting helpers must remain unreachable or be retired; raw header email must never become an authorization shortcut.

sections.title: Production calendar and synced exports
sections.summary: The product direction is one canonical internal production schedule, with external calendars treated as approved projections rather than a source of truth.

facts.label: Current UI
facts.value: Local production calendar chrome has truthful empty behavior

facts.label: Future delivery
facts.value: Provider, identity, timezone, conflict, retention, and export policy remain owner decisions

body: No calendar provider account, subscription, export, or external write is configured by this repository. The UI must show not configured until server-projected evidence exists.
Calendar synchronization cannot create a competing stage/date record outside the canonical production model.

sections.title: WTF OS MCP, agentic Settings, and client setup
sections.summary: The current `wtf-os-local` server is stateless, STDIO, deterministic, and read-only. Settings and hosted MCP are designed as visible configuration controls, not hidden installers.

facts.label: Local MCP
facts.value: Release status, release history, and copy-only setup guidance are the only exposed tools/resources

facts.label: Hosted MCP
facts.value: A future /mcp Worker needs an owner-approved host, Access/OAuth policy, redacted DTOs, audit model, and deployment

body: Copy prompts for Codex, Cursor, or compatible clients must contain only a local command or an owner-approved placeholder. Copying never mutates a user’s configuration.
There is no global installation, remote MCP endpoint, ChatGPT marketplace publication, or account-management capability in the current checkout.

sections.title: Versioning, release channels, changelog, and future OTA
sections.summary: Packages and the local plugin expose version metadata, while the future release model requires immutable events, approval, signed manifests, rollback, compatibility, staged rollout, and retention before OTA becomes possible.

facts.label: Version sources
facts.value: Root, web, Worker, and plugin versions are independent repository metadata

facts.label: OTA posture
facts.value: Not supported until a native application and signed, tested update channel exist

body: A Git revision, a package version, or an entry in CHANGELOG.md is not a published release. The ledger maintains those distinctions to prevent a false deployment or OTA claim.
Release events must be append-only and store a redacted evidence reference before the current-release projection changes.

sections.title: Verification, CI, environments, and operational safety
sections.summary: Phase 1 and Phase 2 have repository-owned CI workflows and local proof commands. The Phase 3 focused runner is real local regression evidence, not deployment or owner-acceptance proof.

facts.label: CI coverage
facts.value: Phase 1 and Phase 2 workflows are tracked; there is no repository Phase 3 deployment or plugin-release workflow

facts.label: Phase 3 checks
facts.value: Focused Worker/public tests, typecheck, and whitespace checks run through a read-only runner

body: Staging and production access remain separately owner-gated. A local test or green static workflow cannot certify a remote binding, OAuth account, calendar export, application policy, queue, cron, or deployment.
Environment-specific resources must be distinct and credentials must remain outside source control.

sections.title: Continuous architecture and release documentation lifecycle
sections.summary: Architecture changes are reviewed through a structured source ledger and deterministic generator. CI checks that generated HTML and companion inventories match the selected architecture inputs.

facts.label: Update command
facts.value: npm run docs:architecture:update regenerates the HTML and companion inventories

facts.label: Freshness gate
facts.value: npm run docs:architecture:check fails when generated artifacts no longer match source inputs

body: When architecture-affecting code, bindings, migrations, workflows, version metadata, or release metadata changes, update this source ledger for semantic claims and regenerate before review.
Runtime changes remain human-attested: an owner may append a redacted receipt after a separately approved action. CI must never configure Cloudflare, OAuth, calendar, MCP, or OTA state.

drift.title: Historic deployment statements are not current runtime proof
drift.detail: Older Cloudflare and Phase 2 materials record deployment or closure language. The current checkout and handoff do not provide a fresh Access Application, policy, hostname, or runtime receipt.

drift.title: Generated service inventory was incomplete
drift.detail: The prior automated service scan reported no external services despite declared Worker bindings. This generated ledger supersedes that limited scan with evidence-linked facts.
drift.nextGate: Keep the deterministic generator and source review in CI.

drift.title: Phase 3 remains a local recovery
drift.detail: Queue/cron wiring, durable large-media upload, durable ticket single-use, configured asset proof, OAuth connection, and owner acceptance remain open.
drift.nextGate: Separate owner-approved implementation and deployment slices.
